turns.prompt_text: I would like to wear contact lenses but I'm unable to get my ID to open it very far
turns.response_html:
It is very common to struggle with tight eyelids when starting. To get a wider opening, try reaching your non-dominant hand over your forehead to pull your upper eyelid up from the lash line, pinning it against your brow bone. Simultaneously, use the middle finger of your dominant hand to pull your lower lid down.

Quick Tips for Small Openings

  • Dry your fingers: Wet fingers make lids slippery; use a lint-free towel to ensure a firm grip on your skin.
  • Look up: Aim for the white part of your eye rather than the center. Once the lens touches, look down to center it before releasing your lids.
  • Tuck and roll: If the lens is too wide, try tucking the top edge under your upper lid first, then pulling the lower lid over the bottom edge.
  • Use a mirror: Place a mirror flat on a table and lean over it so you are looking straight down; gravity will help the lens stay on your finger.

If you continue to have trouble, you might ask your optometrist about smaller diameter lenses or Rigid Gas Permeable (RGP) lenses, which are physically smaller than standard soft contacts.
